description: B-25J-30-NC delivered to the USAAF 2 July 1945; civil-registered N9167Z from 1963 and N345BG from March 1993; acquired by the museum in 2010 and comprehensively restored at Aero Trader in Chino California over the winter of 2011 and 2012 before arriving at Port Clinton in 2012; kept airworthy and flown to airshows so it is not always physically at the museum
aliases: TB-25N; Mitchell; N345BG; N9167Z; B25; B25J; TB25N

description: Museum-owned 1929 Ford Trimotor home-based at Port Clinton and leased to the Experimental Aircraft Association for the Fly the Ford tour so it is frequently away from the museum; also flown under the name City of Wichita

Former Island Airlines Ford Trimotor under long-term restoration in the museum hangar by EAA Tin Goose Chapter 1247 and the Tri-Motor Heritage Foundation; the museum lists it as 5-AT-40 aircraft 13 which mixes a model-line number with a fleet number rather than giving a construction number so no c/n is recorded
General Motors-built Avenger operated by Lake Erie Warbirds in association with the museum and flown to public events so it is not permanently static

Amphibious Catalina purchased in Texas and delivered to Port Clinton in the week before 30 March 2022; reported at the time as one of very few remaining operational PBYs; no civil registration or build date is published by the museum
aliases: OA-10; Catalina; Canso; BuNo 46662; PBY6A; OA10

description: Museum-owned Stearman named in honour of the late local Tuskegee Airman Harold; no serial or registration is published by the museum
Midget class pylon racer raced as number 97 and dating from before 1949; donated to the museum in 2017
aliases: Denight Special; DDT; Midget racer; Race 97
